update_log: Baseline initialization of high-frequency International Boundary Lines (India and Global) for Geography Static GK.

indian_international_boundaries.key_fact: Drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe in 1947 to partition British India into India and Pakistan. The East Radcliffe Line now forms the Indo-Bangladesh border.
Proposed by Sir Henry McMahon at the 1914 Simla Convention. It serves as the de facto boundary in the eastern sector (Arunachal Pradesh). China disputes its legal status.

indian_international_boundaries.demarcated_between: Pakistan and Afghanistan (India shares a small portion)
indian_international_boundaries.key_fact: Demarcated by Sir Mortimer Durand in 1893. India officially shares a 106 km border with Afghanistan along this line in Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir (POK).

A de facto military boundary separating Indian-controlled and Pakistani-controlled parts of Jammu and Kashmir. Originally known as the Ceasefire Line, it was redesignated after the 1972 Simla Agreement.
A demarcation line that separates Indian-controlled territory from Chinese-controlled territory. Formed after the 1962 Sino-Indian War.
Pakistan claims that this parallel should form the boundary in the Sir Creek area of the Rann of Kutch (Gujarat), but India heavily rejects this claim.
A maritime boundary that separates the Indian state of Tamil Nadu from the island nation of Sri Lanka.

global_international_boundaries.key_fact: Established after WWII in 1945 to divide the Korean peninsula. It remains a heavily fortified Demilitarized Zone (DMZ).
The longest undefended international border in the world. Established by the Anglo-American Convention of 1818 and the Oregon Treaty of 1846.
A massive line of concrete fortifications built by France before WWII to prevent German invasion, which the Germans bypassed by going through Belgium.
A defensive wall built by Germany along its western border opposite the French Maginot Line.
A German defensive position built on the western front during WWI. Rendered irrelevant by the Treaty of Versailles.
Runs along the Oder and Neisse rivers. Established at the Potsdam Conference after WWII and recognized by unified Germany in 1990.
A defensive fortification built by Finland to defend against the Soviet Union during the Winter War (WWII).
Divided the two nations based on the 1954 Geneva Accords. It became irrelevant after the unification of Vietnam in 1976.
A border demarcation published by the United Nations in 2000 to determine whether Israel had fully withdrawn from Lebanon.

global_international_boundaries.demarcated_between: Republic of Cyprus and Turkish Cyprus
global_international_boundaries.key_fact: A demilitarized zone patrolled by the United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus (UNFICYP).
Marks a significant portion of the border between Iraq and Iran (and also separates the US states of Louisiana and Mississippi).
